answer_summary: Complex 5 is the neutral dinitrogen-bridged dimolybdenum(0) complex [{Mo(PNP)(N2)2}2(mu-eta1:eta1-N2)]: one intact N2 bridges the two Mo centers and each Mo also carries two terminal end-on N2 ligands.
assumptions: Ideal-gas behavior at the stated 273.15 K and 1.0 bar, using R = 0.08314 L bar mol^-1 K^-1.
The designed gas-uptake clue is interpreted by its primitive whole-molecule stoichiometry: the candidate 5:2 N2:4 ratio predicts a volume inside the printed 94.97 +/- 0.005 cm3 interval.
Reduction of neutral MoCl3(PNP) by three sodium equivalents removes three chloride ligands and gives neutral Mo(0).

PNP remains a neutral tridentate six-electron donor, coordinated N2 remains intact and neutral, each end-on Mo-N2 contact donates two electrons, and the isolated closed-shell product follows the 18-electron rule.
The product is a single molecular species represented by the smallest integral stoichiometric unit, rather than an arbitrary higher oligomer or mixture.
